prompt: How do I create a SharePoint list in SharePoint?
completion:
## How to Create a SharePoint List

Below is a step‑by‑step guide that covers the most common ways to create a **custom list** in SharePoint (modern experience).  
Feel free to skip the sections that don’t apply to your situation.

> **Prerequisites**  
> • You must have **Edit** (or higher) permissions on the site where you want to create the list.  
> • For programmatic methods you’ll need the appropriate PowerShell modules installed or an account with the required rights.

---

### 1. Create a List from the Modern SharePoint UI

#### 1.1. Navigate to the Site
1. Open the SharePoint site where you want the list.  
2. Click the **Settings** gear → **Site contents**.

#### 1.2. Add a New List
1. In **Site contents**, click the **New** button (or **+ New** → **List**).  
2. Pick one of the built‑in templates or choose **Blank list** for a clean slate.  
   - **Blank list**: start with no columns and build from scratch.  
   - **Pre‑built templates**: “Issue tracker”, “Contact list”, “Event list”, etc.

3. Give the list a name (e.g., “Project Tasks”), optionally a description, then click **Create**.

#### 1.3. Add Columns
1. After creation, you’ll land on the list view.  
2. Click **+ Add column** → pick a column type:  
   - **Single line of text**  
   - **Choice** (drop‑down or checkbox)  
   - **Number**  
   - **Date & Time**  
   - **Yes/No** (checkbox)  
   - **Lookup** (pointing to another list)  
   - **Hyperlink or picture**  
   - **Person or Group**  
   - **Calculated** (formula)  
   - **Currency**  
   - …etc.

3. Configure the column: internal name, description, required, default value, etc.  
4. Repeat until all needed columns are added.

#### 1.4. (Optional) Configure List Settings
1. In the list, click the **gear** icon → **List settings** (or **Settings** > **List settings**).  
2. Adjust:
   - **Versioning settings** (enable content approval, keep multiple versions, etc.)  
   - **Content types** (add or remove types)  
   - **Advanced settings** (read‑only, editing restrictions, etc.)  
   - **Permissions** (break inheritance, set unique permissions)  

---

### 2. Create a List in Classic SharePoint (for older tenants or on-prem)

1. Open the site → click **Site contents**.  
2. Click **+ New** → **List**.  
3. Choose a template or “Blank list”, then give it a name.  
4. Add columns via **List Settings** → **Columns** → **Create column**.

The classic UI has similar options, just presented a bit differently.

---

### 3. Create a List Programmatically

#### 3.1. PowerShell + PnP PowerShell (recommended)

```powershell
# Install module if needed
Install-Module -Name PnP.PowerShell

# Connect to the site
Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/YourSite -Interactive

# Create the list
Add-PnPList -Title "Project Tasks" -Template GenericList -Description "Track project tasks"

# Add columns
Add-PnPField -List "Project Tasks" -DisplayName "Task Name" -InternalName "TaskName" -Type Text
Add-PnPField -List "Project Tasks" -DisplayName "Due Date"   -InternalName "DueDate"   -Type DateTime
Add-PnPField -List "Project Tasks" -DisplayName "Status"     -InternalName "Status"     -Type Choice -Choices "Not Started","In Progress","Done"
```

> **Tip**: The `-Template` parameter can be `GenericList`, `IssueTracking`, `Contact`, `Event`, etc., matching the SharePoint list templates.

#### 3.2. SharePoint REST API (for web apps)

```http
POST https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/YourSite/_api/web/lists
Content-Type: application/json;odata=verbose
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

{
  "__metadata": { "type": "SP.List" },
  "AllowContentTypes": true,
  "BaseTemplate": 100,        // 100 = GenericList
  "ContentTypesEnabled": true,
  "Description": "List created via REST",
  "Title": "REST Tasks"
}
```

After creating the list, you can POST to `/web/lists/getByTitle('REST Tasks')/fields` to add columns.

---

### 4. Create a List From Excel (Using Power Automate)

1. In the list view, click **New** → **Import from Excel** (available in modern lists).  
2. Upload a CSV/Excel file that matches the column structure.  
3. Power Automate will create the list automatically and populate it.  

> **Prerequisite**: The Excel file must have a header row that defines column names.

---

### 5. Quick Checklist for a New List

| Step | What to Do | Tips |
|------|------------|------|
| 1 | Name & description | Keep it concise but descriptive. |
| 2 | Add columns | Add the most important ones first; you can always add more later. |
| 3 | Set required columns | Prevent blank entries on critical fields. |
| 4 | Enable versioning | Useful for audit trails. |
| 5 | Set permissions | If the list is sensitive, break inheritance and assign unique rights. |
| 6 | Add views | Create “All Items”, “My Items”, “Overdue Tasks”, etc. |
| 7 | Add forms | Customize the New/Edit form with Power Apps if needed. |
| 8 | Automate | Use Power Automate to send emails, update statuses, etc. |

---

## Recap

1. **Modern UI**: `Site contents → New → List → Add columns`.  
2. **Classic UI**: similar steps but via the classic menu.  
3. **PowerShell/PnP**: scriptable for bulk creation or automation.  
4. **REST API / Power Automate**: for developers or when integrating with other services.  

Once your list is created, you can start adding items, set up workflows, create dashboards in Power BI, or embed the list on a SharePoint page. Happy list‑building!
